title: hx-vals & hx-include: Dynamic JSON and Form Payload Serialization

progressiveExplaining.eli5: Normally, a button only submits the inputs inside its own form. If you want a button to grab data from three different inputs scattered across the entire room, `hx-include` gathers them up. And if you want to attach extra hidden secret codes, `hx-vals` stamps them onto the envelope.
progressiveExplaining.junior: `hx-vals` adds extra parameters to an HTMX request: `hx-vals='{"role": "admin", "source": "banner"}'`. For dynamic JavaScript expressions, use `js:` prefix: `hx-vals='js:{timestamp: Date.now()}'`. `hx-include="#other-form, #search-input"` includes the values of external inputs or forms in the current request payload.
progressiveExplaining.senior: Architecturally, `hx-include` and `hx-vals` decouple request payload serialization from DOM tree hierarchy. In standard HTML, an input must be a DOM descendant of a `<form>` to be submitted. `hx-include` accepts any CSS selector, finds all matching form controls, and serializes their names and values into the request (`application/x-www-form-urlencoded` or `multipart/form-data`), enabling complex multi-widget dashboard submissions.
progressiveExplaining.underTheHood: Before dispatching a request, HTMX gathers parameters. First, it serializes the host element/form. Second, it evaluates `hx-include` selectors using `document.querySelectorAll()`, running `serializeForm()` on each match. Third, it parses `hx-vals` (evaluating JS if prefixed with `js:` or `javascript:`), merging all key-value pairs into the outgoing request parameter bag.

interviewGotchas.question: What is the difference between `hx-vals` and `hx-headers`?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Interviewers test your knowledge of HTTP protocol structure within HTMX.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: `hx-vals` adds parameters to the **request body** (for POST/PUT) or query string parameters (for GET). `hx-headers` adds custom **HTTP headers** to the request (e.g. `hx-headers='{"Authorization": "Bearer token"}'` or `{"X-Custom-ID": "123"}`).
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Do not pass authentication tokens into `hx-vals` if your backend middleware expects them in the `Authorization` HTTP header.

interviewGotchas.question: Why must JSON in `hx-vals` use single quotes on the outside and double quotes on the inside?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Checks attention to valid HTML attribute parsing syntax.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: HTML attributes use double or single quotes. Since standard JSON keys and string values *strictly require* double quotes (`{"key": "value"}`), the HTML attribute itself must be wrapped in single quotes: `hx-vals='{"key": "value"}'`. Wrapping in double quotes without escaping will create invalid HTML and cause JSON parsing errors.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: `hx-vals="{'key': 'value'}"` is invalid JSON and will fail to parse.
